title: Supreme Court: Income Tax Reassessment Is Invalid Without a Section 143(2) Notice
case_name: Principal Commissioner of Income Tax, Bhubaneshwar v. Orissa Mining Corporation Ltd.
card_summary: The Supreme Court held that a Section 143(2) notice is mandatory before completing reassessment under Section 147, dismissing the Revenue's appeals against the Orissa High Court. It rejected the argument that a Section 142(1) letter asking for information could substitute for the notice. Section 292BB cures only certain service defects, not its complete absence, and the taxpayer's participation does not excuse this.
card_tip: Check the assessment file for a Section 143(2) notice before defending a reassessment on the ground that the taxpayer took part in the proceedings; participation does not cure its absence.
verification_notes: Confirmed by numerous independent reports (LiveLaw, Verdictum, Taxscan, LiveLawBiz and others) agreeing on parties, citation, bench (Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva) and holding; judgment itself not accessed.
